conclusions: Existing native test bodies and payroll/history browser fixture bytes are preserved; only the shared runner entry union changes before the appended tax scenario.

The new browser fixture imports the actual TaxPreparationsWorkspace and tax HTTP client. Named export, props, labels, buttons and lookup form selectors match the current author implementation and author confirmation.

The fetch wrapper permits same-origin company API requests and forwards them to the real compiled company router with explicitly synthetic test actor identity. A successful first creation response is fully consumed before it is deliberately lost, making the retry exercise a committed operation.

The browser requires two POSTs with identical request IDs, visible native readback, disappearance of preparer controls and previous values on actor/role change, a real submitter lookup without taxpayer identity, and cleared result/lookup state on company change.

Native database assertions require exactly one stored input with the entered taxpayer/year/pence, zero inputs in the second company, one creation receipt, two prepare receipts and an audited submitter read.

The existing runner remains loopback-only with a fresh temporary browser profile, a 45-second bound and process/directory cleanup. It uses the existing guarded disposable PostgreSQL test runner and compiled production routes; no production or external identity provider is contacted.

The added scenario emits fixed allowlisted stage names and boolean success only. It does not log credentials, request bodies, taxpayer identifiers or amounts; the stored-field assertion is boolean and the fixtures are synthetic.
